title: Context and System Fusion in Post-ASR Emotion Recognition with Large Language Models

live_model.evidence: 'Specifically, gpt-4o-2024-05-13 and gpt-3.5-turbo-0125 with temperature=1, max tokens=250, seed=42' (footnote 5, Section 4.1)

prompt.location: Fig. 1 (context-size-2 template) and Fig. 2 (context 4 plus 5 ASR outputs); system message 'You are a helpful assistant.'
prompt.note: Template text is in the extracted file; labels restricted to anger/happiness/sadness/neutral in square brackets.

claim.metric: unweighted accuracy (training set, CW=0, ASR selection 'longest and most punc')
claim.location: Table 1, column gpt-4o, row CW 0 (CW 16: 0.575); Table 3 best fusion 0.594

data.source: GenSEC Task 3 (github.com/YuanGongND/llm_speech_emotion_challenge), IEMOCAP re-split by organizers; 2,577 training utterances need predictions; test references held by organizers

notes: IEMOCAP-derived challenge data require the IEMOCAP license agreement; reported numbers are on the training set with temperature 1 sampling.

resolution.plan: The training-set utterances (5,225, of which 2,577 need predictions), the 11 ASR hypotheses per utterance, speaker sex and emotion labels are distributed by the GenSEC Task 3 challenge repository (IEMOCAP-derived, license-gated). Build the Fig. 1/2 template with CW=0 and the 'longest and most punctuated' ASR selection, run gpt-4o-2024-05-13 with temperature 1, max tokens 250, seed 42 and the system message 'You are a helpful assistant.', and compute unweighted accuracy vs Table 1 (0.449). The authors' code is at github.com/rggdmonk/GenSEC-Task-3.
resolution.approximation: Temperature-1 sampling; IEMOCAP license agreement needed for the challenge data.
